scope: Local Store canonical Session outcome context, historical attribution and restart, current owner/recipient audience filtering, exact delivery selection validation, and existing provider-chat/membership integration. No new canonical server/provider media journey qualification.
behavior: ContextView now selects authoritative session_control journal outcomes in addition to its existing message, Session and artifact sources. Each canonical outcome contains its original SessionView state/revision and creator/source-owner attribution. Later acceptance/end and restart do not rewrite earlier invite or accept outcomes.

Both current principals, resource audiences and recipient ceilings filter before selection limits and omitted counts. A newer owner/human-only Session cannot hide a shared AI Session by consuming the shared page limit, expose its body or alter omitted counts.

Canonical delivery admission reconstitutes the exact historical body from the referenced journal event rather than checking it against the current Session projection. A substituted current body or unrelated source is refused.

A failing regression demonstrated that an authorized canonical journal position could previously be relabeled session_ready and paired with current metadata, creating a pending receipt. Admission now binds the actual journal kind as well as position/source/body; the same regression refuses the relabeling.

Existing discovery/delivery pagination, membership and provider-chat recovery/privacy tests pass. Three new library regressions are included once in the full650 library total. Three intentionally ignored standalone subprocess helper entrypoints remain exercised through parent tests.
preliminary_observations: The initial new test used optional rather than concrete Session End reason fields and failed to compile. This was a fixture error, corrected before runtime qualification.

The first outcome test assumed contiguous revisions. Actual public control results report their observed revisions; the final regression compares every snapshot to its corresponding public result rather than inventing revision increments.
The relabeling regression failed with an actual admitted receipt before the kind-binding fix and passes after it. That failing result is retained as defect evidence, not counted as a pass.

Two older membership fixtures duplicated Session presence already created by public acceptance. They now assert existing presence, explicitly adjust the selected role where needed, and select the intended participant/epoch rather than an arbitrary first row. Their original role/removal invariants remain. Only this integration test file changed during the unchanged-library full run; its final own compiled suite is separately recorded.
Inactive superseded generated incremental sessions were removed with a local manifest to preserve build space. No source, raw log or built test executable was removed by that cleanup.

The generated HTTP reference still described telephone movement as unfinished after G6-041 completion. Its generator and generated reference now describe the recorded native/telephone movement scope and retain later browser/remote/provider qualifications.
not_qualified: G6-042 is not complete. Explicit canonical multi-participant assistant/session destination binding, fresh/existing assistant provider initialization/export and exact acknowledgment/rejection/truncation/incompleteness journeys remain to implement/qualify.

The complete public-context call -> private-only consultation -> attributable follow-up after restart must run through actual canonical server/client and designated provider interfaces. This Store checkpoint does not substitute for that journey.

Ordinary older Session/artifact projection paths still need reconciliation with the host-context contract that specifies saved event snapshots; this phase adds canonical Session outcomes only. Task recall deliberately retains its separately documented current-metadata semantics.
No new SIP/Core/media/server runtime, Linux/browser/remote/provider/PSTN, performance, independent acceptance or publication qualification is claimed.
